recommendations.headline: Satisfaction, not price, is the real conversion lever: satisfied calls close at 71% vs 15% for neutral and 5% for dissatisfied calls, yet 51% of calls (1,397) are merely neutral and price is often never even discussed (71%, 1,923 calls).
behaviour: Price enquiry is the top intent (926 of 2,716 calls, 34%) and price_shopper (467) / comparing_quotes (280) are common behaviours, yet price is only actually discussed in 29% of calls and 'too_high' is flagged in just 84 calls.
Callback (1,258, 46%) far exceeds actual order (525, 19%), showing most customers stall rather than buy on the first call.
Stock_availability (360) and delivery_time (219) objections are nearly as frequent as price_high (363), showing logistics concerns rival pricing.
Repeat buyers (244) and bulk buyers (236) are sizeable segments but 'loyal_to_us' is tagged only 22 times, suggesting loyalty isn't being reinforced.
Needs for fast_delivery (493) and stock_availability (490) outrank even technical_advice (451), showing speed/availability drive decisions as much as product fit.
satisfaction: Only 36% of calls end 'satisfied' (969) vs 51% 'neutral' (1,397) and 8% 'dissatisfied' (228) - most interactions are flat, not delighting customers.
Win rate tracks satisfaction almost linearly: 71% (satisfied) vs 15% (neutral) vs 5% (dissatisfied) - satisfaction is the strongest predictor of conversion in the data.

Price is rarely the stated blocker: 'not_discussed' in 71% of calls (1,923) and 'too_high' in only 3% (84), while rep execution gaps (slow/unclear answers 442, no fixed follow-up 423) are far more common issues.
Price_high objection still wins only 27% of the time and competitor_cheaper only 21%, showing price objections are handled weakly even when raised.

conversion.title: Fix slow/unclear answers on calls
conversion.evidence: 442 calls flagged slow_or_unclear_answer - the single biggest rep gap, and satisfaction is the top driver of win rate (71% vs 15%).
conversion.action: Train reps on quick, confident spec/price responses; use scripted answers for common product questions to cut hesitation.

conversion.title: Always set a fixed follow-up time
conversion.evidence: 423 calls had no_follow_up_fixed; callback is the outcome in 46% of calls (1,258) but many likely go cold.
conversion.action: Mandate every rep to confirm a specific day/time for the next contact and log it for manager tracking.

conversion.title: Send quotes immediately, not 'later'
conversion.evidence: 258 calls had no_quote_sent despite price_enquiry being 34% of all calls.
conversion.action: Use WhatsApp quote templates so reps can send pricing/specs within the call, not as a promised follow-up.

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order
conversion.evidence: 250 calls had didnt_ask_for_order; order outcome is only 19% despite 593 calls tagged as order intent.
conversion.action: Coach reps to close every qualified call with a direct ask ('shall I book this for you?').

conversion.title: Offer alternatives when stock is short
conversion.evidence: 153 calls had didnt_offer_alternative; stock_availability is a top objection (360) with only 25% win rate.
conversion.action: Build a quick-reference cross-brand/size substitution list (e.g., Color On Plus for Radiance) for reps to use live.

conversion.title: Qualify segment and requirement early
conversion.evidence: 'Unknown' segment (1,009 calls) converts at only 25% vs dealer's 40%; didnt_ask_requirement flagged 106 times.
conversion.action: Add a mandatory opening question to identify customer type (dealer/fabricator/contractor) and exact requirement before quoting.

conversion.title: Prioritise dealer relationships
conversion.evidence: Dealers are the largest segment (1,278 calls, 47%) and convert best (40%) among known segments.
conversion.action: Assign dedicated reps/managers to top dealers for faster, personalised service.

offers.title: Cut-to-size / express dispatch service
offers.why: fast_delivery is the top need (493 mentions), cutting_processing need (113) and multiple success stories show same-day/before-lunch delivery wins orders.

offers.title: Technical consultation line for specs/drawings
offers.for_whom: Fabricators and contractors needing custom sheets/flashing
offers.why: needs_technical_help (403) and technical_advice (451) are among top needs; many calls involve drawings, bends and GSM clarifications.

offers.title: Sample dispatch program
offers.why: samples need (72) and quality_doubt objection (101) recur; several call summaries show samples requested before large orders.

offers.title: Standardised credit/payment terms (to evaluate)
offers.why: credit_terms objection (80) has the highest win rate among objections (29%), and needs_credit (103) / credit_period (94) are notable needs.

offers.title: Dedicated bulk/project quote desk
offers.why: bulk_buyer (236) and comparing_quotes (280) behaviours are common; faster structured quotes could reduce drop-off to callback (46% of calls).

offers.title: Proactive stock/price update alerts
offers.why: regular_updates need (215) and repeat_buyer behaviour (244) show demand for staying informed without calling in.

loyalty.title: Formal repeat-buyer recognition
loyalty.how: Track repeat/bulk buyers in CRM and give priority handling (faster callbacks, dedicated contact).
loyalty.why: Repeat_buyer (244) and bulk_buyer (236) are large segments but loyal_to_us is tagged only 22 times, showing an untapped loyalty gap.

loyalty.title: Formalise the gift/scheme program
loyalty.how: Set a clear, consistent schedule for seasonal gifts (e.g., Diwali) and welding rod/sheet schemes communicated in advance.
loyalty.why: Customers explicitly ask about pending gifts and reduced promotional items, indicating these build goodwill and are noticed when missing.

loyalty.title: Referral incentive (non-cash)
loyalty.how: Offer priority service or recognition for customers who refer others, formalising informal referrals.
loyalty.why: Referral behaviour already present (30 calls) despite no formal program.

loyalty.title: Dedicated account manager for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a named point of contact for high-volume dealers to handle PO, payment and delivery queries directly.
loyalty.why: Dealers are 47% of calls and the best-converting known segment (40% win); several summaries show confusion from being passed between reps.

loyalty.title: After-sales support follow-up calls
loyalty.how: Schedule a courtesy call after large orders to confirm satisfaction and invoice/certificate needs.
loyalty.why: after_sales_support (48) and test_certificate (22) needs appear, and dissatisfied calls convert poorly later (5% win).

non_price_benefits.title: Fast, reliable delivery commitments
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery is the top need (493) and multiple successful calls hinge on same-day/before-lunch delivery promises being kept.

non_price_benefits.title: Cutting and custom-size processing
non_price_benefits.why: cutting_processing need (113) and several won calls involve bespoke bends/lengths (e.g., 15ft sheets cut to 4 pieces).

non_price_benefits.title: Strong technical/spec guidance
non_price_benefits.why: needs_technical_help (403) and technical_advice (451) are major needs; reps who clarified specs (GSM, bend, thickness) closed deals.

non_price_benefits.title: Multi-brand flexibility
non_price_benefits.why: When a preferred brand (e.g., Radiance 50 micron) was unavailable, reps successfully offered Color On Plus alternatives, closing the sale.

non_price_benefits.title: Quality assurance and certification support
non_price_benefits.why: quality_assurance (134) and test_certificate (22) needs, plus quality_doubt objection (101), show trust-building documentation helps win and retain.

non_price_benefits.title: Consistent supply reliability
non_price_benefits.why: consistent_supply need (126) and stock_availability objection (360, only 25% win) show dependable stock is a differentiator worth highlighting proactively.

top_questions.question: What is the rate/price for this sheet or screw?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm exact spec (thickness, size, brand) first, then give a prompt, written quote via WhatsApp rather than a 'check and call back' promise.

top_questions.question: Can the price be reduced / matched to a competitor?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the comparison, pivot to delivery speed, quality assurance and service reliability rather than only discussing rate.

top_questions.question: Do you have stock available right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a real-time stock answer where possible; if unavailable, immediately offer an alternative brand/size instead of ending the call.

top_questions.question: Can delivery happen today/tomorrow morning/by a specific time?
top_questions.answer_tip: Set a clear, realistic delivery commitment and confirm cutoff/dispatch times rather than leaving it vague.

top_questions.question: Which brand is better / is this genuine (e.g., JSW vs Silveron)?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain certification and quality credentials confidently to address quality_doubt (101 mentions).

top_questions.question: Can you send the quotation/photos on WhatsApp?
top_questions.answer_tip: Use ready quote and photo templates to respond within the call, avoiding the no_quote_sent gap (258 calls).

top_questions.question: What are the credit/payment terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Clearly explain current advance/balance policy; flag to management that credit_terms objections convert well (29%) and could be formalised.

top_questions.question: Can the sheet be cut/customised to a specific length or bend?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm the cutting/customisation capability clearly and give realistic turnaround, as this often converts urgent/project buyers.
